REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - NOVEMBER 7, 2016 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF AN ADJOURNED REGULAR MEETING AND A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON NOVEMBER 7, 2016, IN THE COUNCIL
CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS,
CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Recreation Services Division Volunteer
  Carly Ng.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in
  attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Carol Chen
  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair George Ray

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  None.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Andrew Johnson III spoke about the homelessness and panhandling
  occurring in the City.

  Herbie J. Pilate, patron and contributor of the Arts, expressed concern
  regarding closure of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts.

  Jay Gray spoke regarding the proposed sales tax measure, the reduction of
  the Council's travel budget, auto allowances for Commission members,
  mileage reimbursement, and funds placed in the budget for unfilled positions.

  Ram Kakkar proposed a Citizen's Review Board to review the City budget.

  Gail Grossman spoke in support of the dissolution of the Commissions and
  Committees and suggested they be dissolved after the next City Council
  reorganization. She spoke in opposition to proposed sales tax measure.

  Steven Likens expressed concern regarding closure of the Cerritos Center for
  the Performing Arts.

  Deborah Broches expressed concern regarding closure of the Cerritos Center
  for the Performing Arts.
 City of Cerritos  November 7, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 5

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  October 27, 2016 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of October 27, 2016
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated November 7,
  2016 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated November 7, 2016 in the
  amount of $6,175,869.54 (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of the Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending September 30, 2016
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending September 30, 2016
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS AUTHORIZING UTILIZATION OF FISCAL YEAR 2017-2018
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS TO IMPROVE
  ACCESSIBILITY TO PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT LOCATED AT LOMA PARK.*

  *Funding is based on an estimate of $164,494 anticipated CDBG funds for Fiscal
  Year 2017-2018. Final CDBG fund allocation may vary.

  A staff report was given by, Eduardo Vega, Associate Planner. A PowerPoint
  Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.
 City of Cerritos  November 7, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 5

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  Ram Kakkar suggested that CDBG funds be utilized for a variety of accessibility
  services, including services for those with hearing loss.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments and the public hearing.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to waive full reading of
  and adopt Resolution No. 2016-23, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS AUTHORIZING UTILIZATION OF FISCAL YEAR 2017-2018
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS TO IMPROVE
  ACCESSIBILITY TO PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT LOCATED AT LOMA PARK
  (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration for repairs to C-1 water well engine overhaul by a sole
  source provider (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vince Brar, Senior Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Chen, and seconded by Pulido, to:

  1. Make a finding that the engine overhaul repairs to the C-1 Water Well are
  necessary to ensure reliability of the City’s drinking water supply; and
  2. Authorize the expenditure of $15,146.58 to Waukesha Pearce Industries for C-1
  Water Well repairs; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute changes in the scope of
  work and related expenses if necessary (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS ADOPTING THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Rebecca Scott, Management Analyst.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.
 City of Cerritos  November 7, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 5

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Pulido, to waive full
  reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2016-24, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS ADOPTING THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN (COUNCIL).
  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration to waive full reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  1009, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS,
  CALIFORNIA, MOVING THE DATE OF THE CITY’S GENERAL MUNICIPAL
  ELECTION FROM THE FIRST TUESDAY AFTER THE FIRST MONDAY IN MARCH
  OF ODD-NUMBERED YEARS TO THE SECOND TUESDAY OF APRIL IN ODD-
  NUMBERED YEARS; or waive full reading and adopt resolutions calling the
  election (consolidated or stand-alone) or introduce an ordinance selecting an
  alternate date for the 2017 Cerritos General Municipal Election (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk.

  Mel Cortez spoke in opposition to moving the election date and spending
  funds to conduct a stand-alone election.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no further individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to waive full
  reading and adopt Ordinance No. 1009, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, MOVING THE
  DATE OF THE CITY’S GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION FROM THE
  FIRST TUESDAY AFTER THE FIRST MONDAY IN MARCH OF ODD-
  NUMBERED YEARS TO THE SECOND TUESDAY OF APRIL IN ODD-
  NUMBERED YEARS (COUNCIL). The motion carried (4 – 1, Pulido “no”) as
  follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  Pulido
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the
  State or Federal Legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for
  signature.

  None.

  Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Pulido, Chen, and Edwards, and
  Mayor Ray.

12.  Closed Session

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting was adjourned at 8:50 p.m., in memory of Janet Gray.
